findings.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` is destructured from a possibly-empty array, then dereferenced as `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining (was `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`). Any Google Meet booking by an organizer with no destination calendar — the exact case this line exists to rescue — throws `TypeError` and 500s instead of falling back to Cal Video. `handleNewBooking:1067` emits `null` and every other builder emits `[]`, so both feed it.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — `deleteEvent` fallback `destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is tautologically dead — it only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it searches for `externalId === undefined` and always returns undefined. `calendarId` degrades to `"primary"`, Google 404s, line 335 swallows the 404 with `resolve()`, and cancellation reports success while the event stays on the host's calendar permanently.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — Same dead predicate in `updateEvent`, but with no `"primary"` default — `calendarId: undefined` is sent to `calendar.events.update`. Rescheduling any booking whose reference lacks `externalCalendarId` now fails outright where it previously fell back to `destinationCalendar.externalId`.

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221` + `office365:73`, `lark:125`, `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:124 — `Calendar.createEvent` gained `credentialId`, but only the Google adapter consumes it. Office365/Lark/CalDAV still resolve `destinationCalendar[0]`. TypeScript accepts the narrower signature so there is **no compile error** — instead EventManager calls each adapter once per destination, and every iteration writes to host 1's calendar using hosts 2..N's credentials. The multi-host fix is inert for every non-Google provider.

packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156 — CalDAV/Apple `createEvent` filters `calendars` against host 1's `externalId`; for host 2's credential the filter matches nothing, `responses` is `[]`, `responses.some(r => !r.ok)` is false, and it returns a success object with a fresh uid though nothing was written. A BookingReference is persisted pointing at an event that exists on no server.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:208 — `updateLocation` writes `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` / `credentialId: result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` (`CalendarManager.ts:312-322`) never populates either — only `createEvent` was updated. `editLocation.handler.ts:120` persists these as fresh references, so every location edit permanently degrades the booking into the legacy no-credential path.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` hard-wires the **video** branch to `undefined` (was `: result.credentialId`). `_video` references get `credentialId: null`, so `handleCancelBooking.ts:491` never fires and Zoom/other meetings are silently never deleted on cancellation.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:541 — `result.push(updateEvent(credential, ...))` sits **outside** the `if (credential)` guard, unlike the parallel `createAllCalendarEvents:369`. A revoked credential passes `undefined` into `updateEvent`, which dereferences `credential.appName`; the throw is caught at :593 and converts *every* reference to `success: false`. One stale host credential fails the whole reschedule for all hosts.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently no-ops when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` — exactly what lines 1063-1067 produce when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. The PR's headline feature fails closed with no log, producing precisely the pre-PR behavior.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:592 — `console.error(message)` was deleted from the rewritten `updateAllCalendarEvents` catch while `message` is still built. Every failure there — Prisma errors, missing credentials, thrown `updateEvent` — is now completely silent.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:597 — The catch returns `[]` when the throw preceded `calendarReference` assignment, where the old code always returned one `success: false` result. Callers gate on `results.every(res => !res.success)`, so an empty array reads as "no failure" and a genuine calendar outage is reported as a fully successful booking.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:758 — The new `loadUsers` catch swallows the original error with no logging and remaps everything: `HttpError` and Prisma errors → client-facing 400 (downgrading deeper status codes), everything else → generic 500. Infrastructure failures are misreported as bad client requests and stacks are discarded.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:724 — The `loadUsers` rewrite drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-user `findMany` select — a field `IsFixedAwareUser` (line 355) declares as required. Unrelated to threading destinationCalendar.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — Drive-by rewrite `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` → `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` **inverts the condition** — a semantic flip in org slug/billing handling smuggled into a calendar PR under cover of a cosmetic spread cleanup.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449 — The recurring-cancellation block (credentials × updatedBookings) is now nested inside the new per-reference loop at :423, so it re-executes fully for every calendar reference. R hosts × C credentials × B bookings instead of C×B (e.g. 180 API calls instead of 60), with latency multiplied by R since each `Promise.all` is awaited inside the sequential outer loop.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:370 — `createAllCalendarEvents` awaits `createEvent` serially per destination. Each is a 300ms–1s external API round trip on the booking-creation critical path; a 6-host collective event adds several seconds. The sibling `else` branch at :380 already uses `Promise.all`.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:380 — The credential-less branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the third `externalId` argument, so `result.externalId` is `undefined` and references persist with no `externalCalendarId` (previously sourced from `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) — feeding the broken `"primary"` delete path in #2.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — The credential-hydration block (`findUnique` + `app.slug` include + 8-field manual remap) is byte-for-byte duplicated at `EventManager.ts:344-368` and `:517-541`, with a third **already-divergent** copy at `handleCancelBooking.ts:433` that omits the `app` include entirely. It has drifted before the PR even merged.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:357 — The hydrated credential is a hand-rolled object literal rather than a shared Prisma select/mapper. New `Credential` columns must be added to every literal by hand, and optional ones are silently dropped at runtime with no type error.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:118 — The comment says "as a fallback we will only check the first one" directly above code that has no fallback and throws on empty — while every other `mainHostDestinationCalendar` site in this PR does use `?.`.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:336 — Multi-destination create returns N `EventResult`s whose `externalId`/`credentialId` pairing builds the booking references consumed by all later update/cancel flows — with no test anywhere asserting the pairing is correct. Wrong pairing silently orphans calendar events.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:343 — The DB credential fallback is new I/O on the booking hot path, exercised only in the team-member case this PR exists for, with zero coverage — `packages/core` has no unit-test or prisma-mock infrastructure at all.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:418 — Cancellation changed `find` → `filter` + per-reference loop with no test asserting one `deleteEvent` per reference. Under-deletion leaves ghost events on co-hosts' calendars; over-deletion spams provider APIs.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — `createAllCalendarEvents` loads a credential by `destination.credentialId` with no check that the credential's owner owns that `DestinationCalendar` or is a host of this event. This deliberately escapes the `this.calendarCredentials` boundary built from vetted organizer/team credentials; the only remaining guard is the integrity of the `credentialId` column, never re-validated.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:517 — Same unscoped `findUnique` in `updateAllCalendarEvents`, driven by `BookingReference.credentialId`. Reschedule/edit-location/confirm are attendee-triggerable, so a poisoned or stale `credentialId` lets the update path act on a non-participant's calendar.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:433 — Ownership scoping (`bookingToDelete.user.credentials.find`) is now only a fast path; on a miss it falls back to an unscoped `findUnique` and calls `deleteEvent` with that credential's token. Cancellation is reachable by anyone holding a booking `uid`, so the "only act with the booking owner's tokens" invariant is gone.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:993 — For `schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"`, every user in `users.slice(1)` has their personal destination calendar written to — but in the dynamic-booking branch `users` comes from caller-supplied `dynamicUserList`, not a vetted host list. If the default dynamic event carries COLLECTIVE, an unauthenticated `POST /api/book/event` could force calendar inserts into arbitrary named users' calendars. *(`packages/lib/defaultEvents.ts` absent from this checkout — unconfirmed.)*

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:2124 — Partial-failure detection is still `results.every(res => !res.success)` while `referencesToCreate` maps *all* results including failures. With N calendars, 1-of-3 success is now the common case: the booking reports full success, sends confirmations, and persists references with `uid: ""` for calendars never written. Nothing is rolled back and no BrokenIntegrationEmail fires.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1877 — Only `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` is connected to the Booking row (schema FK is still single). Every flow that rehydrates a `CalendarEvent` from the booking — reschedule, cancel, payment webhooks, cron reminder — reconstructs a one-element array, so the additional hosts' calendars are permanently lost for already-persisted bookings.

apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249 — The payload is built by spreading `CalendarEvent`, so `destinationCalendar` in outward-facing BOOKING_CREATED/REJECTED/CANCELLED webhooks changed from object to array with no version bump or changelog. Subscribers reading `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` now get `undefined`.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1067 — The empty case is serialized inconsistently: `handleNewBooking` emits `null` while confirm/editLocation/requestReschedule/cancel/deleteCredential/payment-webhooks/cron all emit `[]`. Visible in the snapshots themselves — `webhook.e2e.ts:119` still asserts `null`, `:249` now asserts `[]`. Consumers must handle three shapes.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:121 — The organizer attendee's `email` still comes from `mainHostDestinationCalendar` (index 0) even though the event is inserted into the `credentialId`-matched calendar at :147. Events created on host B's calendar carry host A's organizer address.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063 — When `eventType.destinationCalendar` is set it replaces the organizer's personal calendar, but the `users.slice(1)` loop still adds every other host's personal calendar. Hosts 2..N get events on both team and personal calendars while the organizer gets nothing on theirs — an asymmetry nobody configured and none can disable.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:376 — The credential-less branch now runs once per destination and fans out over all matching credentials each time. Three legacy `DestinationCalendar` rows produce three duplicate events on the organizer's `primary` calendar plus three references with `externalCalendarId: undefined`.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:356 — `if (credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug)` silently skips the destination when a credential exists without a linked app row — no log, no error, no entry in `createdEvents` (same at :529). The `?? ""` on the next line suggests the author was unsure the slug could be absent.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:369 — A destination whose credential resolves nowhere is skipped with no log and no failure result; the unguarded `findUnique` inside the loop can also throw after earlier destinations already created events, leaving orphans with no references — so cancellation can never clean them up.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:442 — If a reference's `credentialId` resolves to no credential — the common case for another host's credential on a collective booking — the reference is skipped with no log and nothing pushed to `apiDeletes`. Cancellation reports success while the event survives.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344` / `:517 — `EventManager` is constructed only from the organizer's credentials, so for a collective event *every* non-organizer destination misses the in-memory list. This is a guaranteed N−1 serialized DB round trips per booking, not a rare fallback; should be one batched `findMany({ where: { id: { in: ids } } })`.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:992 — `schedulingType` is compared as the raw string `"COLLECTIVE"` at :992/:1021/:1077 and via `["COLLECTIVE","ROUND_ROBIN"].includes()` at :689, while :805 still uses the imported `SchedulingType` enum. Mixing defeats rename/exhaustiveness protection.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — The `[mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ...` destructure is repeated at 12 sites across 5 files in three different spellings, with no shared helper — no single place to change "which calendar does a non-multi-host adapter use".

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:989 — `teamMemberPromises` is a `.map` whose async callback pushes into the outer `teamDestinationCalendars`; the array is only safe to read after `await Promise.all` at :1006. Nothing expresses this temporal coupling — memoizing or moving the mapping silently yields an empty array at :1078.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:727 — `throw new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` is thrown inside the `try` that catches it, and the catch preserves messages only for `HttpError`/Prisma errors — so this diagnostic is *always* converted to a generic 500.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063 — The `/** For team events & dynamic collective events, we will need to handle each member destinationCalendar eventually */` TODO was deleted, but the booking still persists only `destinationCalendar[0].id` — signalling the limitation is resolved when only half of it is.

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:182 — `schedulingType` is added to the shared `CalendarEvent`, populated at `handleNewBooking:1074`, and read nowhere. A write-only field on a type consumed by every adapter and email template invites divergent interpretations.

apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:81 — All three webhook assertions use `toMatchObject`, which ignores extra keys — so the newly shipped `schedulingType` field on every outbound webhook payload has no test asserting it. The only tests covering a public contract are structurally incapable of detecting added fields.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:656 — Claim: `Promise.allSettled` over N deletes rejects on first failure, skipping `sendCancelledEmails` while still returning 200. **Note:** `allSettled` never rejects, so the stated mechanism is wrong; the surrounding concern (no retry, no surfacing of failed deletes across N calendars) still holds. Verify before acting.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:551 — `updateEvent` promises are pushed into `result` and awaited only at the end; an intervening `await` in the `newBookingId` merge block can throw first, so `Promise.all(result)` is never reached and in-flight rejections become unhandled.

packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:285 — `log.error(..., credential)` logs the whole credential including `credential.key` (OAuth tokens). Unchanged line, but credentials reaching it now include *other users'* credentials via the new fallback — so it can spill an unrelated host's tokens.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — `evt.destinationCalendar` is built with no de-duplication and no team-size cap; it directly drives one DB lookup + one API round trip per element. Hosts sharing a calendar produce redundant work.
packages/core/EventManager.ts:64 — `EventManagerUser.destinationCalendar` is still `DestinationCalendar

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:370` et al. — Unrelated drive-by churn: `orginalBookingDuration` rename, "organiser"→"organizer" (`CalendarManager.ts:230`), "behaviour"→"behavior" comment, the `import { Prisma, Booking }` type-only split, added `firstName: ""`/`lastName: ""`. Each adds diff noise and misleading `git blame`.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new `deleteEvent` fallback is:

```ts
const calendarId = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

That `find(...)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it searches for `cal.externalId === undefined` (or `null`). In normal cases calendar `externalId` values are defined strings, so this will return `undefined` and fail to select the intended destination calendar. This is a real, verifiable correctness bug introduced by the diff. (The downstream effects about 404 handling/success reporting may depend on code not shown here, but the dead/incorrect fallback logic itself is clearly present.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — Same dead predicate in `updateEvent`, but with no `"primary"` default — `calendarId: undefined` is sent to `calendar.events.update`. Rescheduling any booking whose reference lacks `externalCalendarId` now fails outright where it previously fell back to `destinationCalendar.externalId`.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the new fallback is:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (undefined/null), the predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` compares against that same undefined/null value, which will typically match nothing and return `undefined`. Unlike `createEvent`, `updateEvent` does not apply a `|| "primary"` default before calling `calendar.events.update`, so it can send `calendarId: undefined`.

Previously it would fall back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (single object) and avoid this. This is a concrete, diff-verifiable regression that can break updates/reschedules when no `externalCalendarId` is present.
